## 1. Introduction/Context

South  East  Technological  University  (SETU)  is  committed  to  creating  a  supportive  and inclusive work environment that recognises the diverse needs of its staff. As part of this commitment, the Leave Management Policy provides clear guidelines and procedures for accessing and managing various types of leave entitlements. This policy ensures that staff have the flexibility to balance their work responsibilities with personal, family, and healthrelated needs, while maintaining consistency and fairness in the application of leave across SETU.

The Leave Management Policy applies to all eligible staff members at SETU and outlines the specific types of leave available, including annual leave, sick leave, parental leave, and other statutory  and  discretionary  leave  options.  By  setting  out  a  transparent  and  consistent approach to leave entitlements, SETU aims to promote staff well-being, enhance work-life balance,  and  support  the  operational  needs  of  SETU.  This  policy  aligns  with  current employment  legislation.  Links  to  all  relevant  circulars  and  legislation  referenced  in  this policy are contained in each section below.

## 2. Purpose

The primary objective of SETU Leave Management Policy is to ensure staff are provided with a  reasonable  and  regular  amount  of  rest  and  recreation  away  from  work.  The  Leave Management Policy, operating for all staff in SETU is governed by various circular letters issued by the Department of Further & Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science (DEFERIS)

## 3. Scope

This policy covers all staff members of SETU.  The objective of the policy is to provide staff with details of entitlements to unpaid and paid leave and to advise on the protection of staff member's rights whilst on leave.

The policies and procedures are subject to change from time to time depending on HR and circulars from DEFERIS.

## 4. Principles

The  Leave  Management  Policy  at  SETU  is  designed  to  ensure  a  consistent,  fair,  and transparent approach to the management of various types of leave for all staff.  SETU is committed to  applying  leave  entitlements  consistently  across  all  departments  and  staff members. All requests for leave will be processed in a fair and transparent manner, with clear communication regarding leave entitlements, procedures, and approval timelines.

## 5. Aims of the Policy

The aim of this Policy is to provide clear guidance to all staff regarding their rights and entitlements to various types of leave. It aims to ensure that all  staff members are fully informed about the types of leave available, and the conditions under which they can be taken.  By  doing  so,  this  Policy  ensures  consistency,  transparency,  and  fairness  in  the administration of leave across SETU, while also supporting staff in managing their work-life balance.

## 6. Policy/Procedure

SETU values transparency in its leave management processes. Staff should understand the criteria, procedures, and expectations regarding requesting, approving, and tracking leave.

## 6.1 Sick leave

The university operates a sick leave scheme for staff.

Sick Leave Circular - 0062/2015

Amendments to the Public Service Sick-Leave Regulations Letter - S.I.-124/2014

## 6.2 Unpaid Medical Leave

Staff will be entitled to unpaid medical leave. This leave can be availed of by staff members who need to take time off  work to  deal  with  serious  medical  care  for  a  child  or  other relevant person like a family member.

Work Life Balance and Miscellaneous Provisions Act

## 6.3 Annual Leave

All staff members of SETU are entitled to annual leave.  For Professional, management and support staff, their annual leave entitlement is detailed in their contract of employment and for academic staff in accordance with the academic calendar.  The leave year runs from 1st September to 31st August annually.

Annual Leave - 2016 Circular

In addition to annual leave, all staff are entitled to ten public holidays and Good Friday.  The public holidays are:

- New Year' Day
- St Brigid's Day
- St. Patrick's Day
- Easter Monday
- First Monday in May, June & August
- Last Monday in October
- Christmas Day
- St. Stephen's Day

## 6.4 Shorter Working Year

The shorter working year scheme will allow staff members to apply for special unpaid leave for one or more continuous periods of not less than 2 and not more than 13 weeks at any time during the year.

Shorter Working Year - Circular 14/2009

## 6.5 Assault Leave

Assault Leave/Leave of Absence following Assault. Leave of absence under this scheme may be  granted  to  a  lecturer  who  is  unable  to  perform  their  duties  due  to  a  physical  injury following an assault in the course of the lecturer's duties and during approved activities . Absence Following Assault - Circular 0063/2019

## 6.6 Domestic Violence Leave

Staff members will be entitled to leave with pay, referred to as 'domestic violence leave'. This leave can be availed of by a staff member who is experiencing or has experiencing domestic  violence or  a  staff  member  who  is  supporting  a  'relevant  person'  who  has experienced in the past, or is currently experiencing domestic violence.

Civil Service Policy and Supports Domestic Violence and Abuse

## 6.7 Compassionate Leave

Compassionate leave may be granted to provide staff with time away from work at a time of bereavement in the family.

Compassionate Leave Circular - 01/2017

## 6.8 Force Majeure Leave

The purpose of force majeure leave is to provide paid leave, in the event that a member of a  staff  member's  family  or  co-habitee  has  suffered  an  illness  or  injury  and  the  staff member's presence is urgently required.

Force Majeure Leave is defined under the Parental Leave Act 1998 and the Parental Leave (Amendment) Act of 2006 as a staff member 's entitlement to paid time off for urgent family reasons owing to illness or injury.

Force Majeure and Other Urgent Family Reasons Leave - Circular 05/2010

## 6.9 Carers Leave

The Carers Leave Act, 2001 entitles a staff member to take unpaid leave to enable them to provide full time care and attention for a person who is in need of such care.  The Act protects the employment rights of staff who take Carer's Leave.

Carers Leave Act 2001

## 6.10 Parents Leave

The Act entitles certain staff members who are relevant parents in relation to a child to paid leave (paid by the Department of Social Protection) for the purposes of enabling them to provide, or assist in the provision of, care to the child.

You  may  qualify  for  a  payment  called Parent's  Benefit from  the  Department  of  Social Protection  which  is  paid  to  staff  who  have  made  the  necessary  PRSI  contributions  and satisfy the eligibility criteria for payment.

Parent's  Leave  and  Benefit  Act  2019  amended  by  the    Family  Leave  and  Miscellaneous Provisions Act 2021 provides paid statutory leave for a relevant parent within the first two years of a child's life, or in the case of adoption, within two years of the placement of the child with the family. Parent's leave is available to each parent.

## 6.11 Maternity Leave

Female members of s taff are entitled to 26 consecutive week's leave of absence with full pay.  In addition, an application may be made at the end of paid maternity leave to allow up to 16 weeks special leave without pay.  In order to obtain maternity leave, staff must notify HR of their pregnancy at least 8 weeks prior to their expected date of delivery.

Maternity Protection Act 1994

Maternity Leave to Cover Premature Births in the Civil Service - Circular 10/2019 Maternity and Adoptive Leave for Academic Staff - cl0022/2013

Implementation of the Regulations of the Maternity Protection-Amendment Act 2004

## 6.12 Adoptive Leave

Adoptive leave gives an eligible staff member who is adopting a child, paid consecutive leave from the date the child is placed in their care.

Adoptive Leave Act 1995

## 6.13 Paternity Leave

The Paternity Leave and Benefit Act 2016 commenced on 1 September 2016. It provides statutory  paternity  leave  and  benefit  for  relevant  parents.    Further  information  can  be found at

Paternity Leave Scheme for all Eligible Staff In Institutes of Technology - Circular 0069/2016

## 6.14 Parental Leave

The Parental Leave Act, 1998, as amended by the Parental Leave (Amendment) Act 2006, entitles parents of children to 26 weeks unpaid parental leave to take care of the child up to the age of sixteen.

The Parents Leave and Benefit Act 2019 Parental Leave Amendment Act 2006 Parental Leave Circular - 20/2008 Parental Leave Circular Amendment Letter

## 6.15 Marriage & Civil Partnership Leave

Staff members are entitled to avail of additional leave to facilitate the pre and post events that accompany a Marriage/Civil Partnership.

A staff member will be allowed up to 5 days special leave at the time of marriage subject to an overall total between annual leave and marriage leave of 27 days in the leave year in which the marriage takes place.

Special Leave with Pay on Marriage - Circular 6/2016

## 6.16 Career Break

Staff may avail of career breaks for a minimum period of one year up to a maximum period of five years.  See further information regarding career break policy here SETU | HR policies Career Break Scheme in the Civil Service - Circular 4/2013

## 6.17 Jury Service Leave

Section 29 of the Juries Act 1976, provides that a person in employment is entitled to be released from work for the purpose of jury service.  Where staff are called upon for jury service or to act as a state witness, leave with pay will be given.

Juries Act 1976

## 7. Definition

## Relevant parents:

- A parent of the child
- A spouse, civil partner or cohabitant of the parent of the child
- A parent of a donor-conceived child as provided for under section 5 of the Children and Family Relationships Act 2015
- The adopting parent or parents of a child
- The civil partner or spouse of the child's adopting parent (if the parents have not adopted jointly)

## 8. Compliance

It is expected that all staff of the University will comply with this policy document.

## 11. Responsibility and Authority

Responsibility  for  Leave  Management  at  SETU  is  shared  among  staff  members,  line managers, and the Human Resources department to ensure that leave entitlements are administered  fairly,  consistently,  and  in  compliance  with  SETU  policy  and  relevant legislation. Each party has a distinct role in upholding these standards, contributing to a system that balances individual needs with the operational requirements of SETU.

Staff members are responsible for understanding their leave entitlements and adhering to established procedures for requesting leave. This includes providing appropriate notice, to allow  for  effective  planning  and  continuity  of  operations.  Leave  requests  during  core working  or  teaching  periods  may  require  additional  notice  to  accommodate  the  critical nature of these times and minimise disruption. Staff must also ensure that any required documentation is submitted promptly and communicate openly with their line managers to discuss and resolve any issues related to leave arrangements

Line  managers  are  accountable  for  the  fair  and  timely  consideration  of  leave  requests, assessing them in line with operational needs, and ensuring adherence to policy guidelines. They  are  also  responsible  for  maintaining  accurate  records  of  team  members'  l eave, communicating decisions clearly, and coordinating with HR on any extended absences or complex leave cases that may arise.

The Human Resources department supports line managers and staff by providing guidance on  the  interpretation  and  application  of  leave  entitlements,  ensuring  compliance  with statutory entitlements.

SETU upholds a structured approach to leave management that supports staff well-being while maintaining operational continuity and accountability.

## 12. Policy Review

This Policy will be reviewed every 3 years and in line with appropriate legislation and/or circulars or updates as issued by Department of Public Expenditure, NDP Delivery & Reform, Higher Education Authority or Department of Education & Youth, from time to time.

## 13. Policy Author

The authors of this policy are SETU Human Resources Department. Any feedback or issues arising on implementation of this policy should be communicated to the policy authors. They are responsible to ensure that the Policy Owner is aware of these comments when reviewing the policy.
